title: Ponticianus' story (Confessions 8.6)
hook: a visitor tells of Antony, and Augustine is ashamed he's still stuck
tomorrow: what did a child chant over the garden wall?

segments.voice: Alypius shut his eyes at the games, opened them once, and was hooked. Your line: just one look. Today, a story told in a living room.
screen: `JUST ONE LOOK.` → `A STORY IN A LIVING ROOM.`

segments.voice: A friend finally quits the job she's complained about for years, the same week you're still talking about yours. Augustine got a story like that. A visitor drops by his house in Milan: Ponticianus, a fellow African with a high post at the emperor's court. He spots a book on the game table, picks it up, and smiles. It's the apostle Paul. And he starts telling a story, with no idea what it's about to do to his host.
screen: `SHE FINALLY QUIT.` → `A VISITOR FROM COURT.` → `A BOOK ON THE GAME TABLE.`

segments.voice: First he talks about Antony, the monk of Egypt, amazed they've never heard of him. Then the story he came with. At Trier, he and three companions went walking by the city wall. Two of them wandered into a small house where some servants of God lived, and found a book: the life of Antony. One began to read, and something caught fire. A friend of God, he said, if I want it, look, I become one now. Both stayed. As Ponticianus spoke, Augustine says, God turned him around to face himself. He saw his stalling, and he was ashamed. Years before, he admits, he had prayed: give me chastity and self-control, but not yet. So here's a question churches answer differently. Some tell faith as a moment, a day you can name. Their best case: not yet can be a quiet no, and two officers changed in an afternoon. Others tell it as growth over a lifetime, in prayer, worship and community. Their best case: Augustine had circled for years before this, and those years counted too. Some churches ask for a testimony of the moment you decided; others speak more of a long road. Augustine's story holds both: years of stalling, and a now that's coming.
screen: `LOOK, I BECOME ONE NOW.` · `BUT NOT YET.` · `A MOMENT YOU CAN NAME?` · `OR A LIFETIME OF GROWING?` · then, large: `WHY NOT NOW?`

segments.voice: Get up and walk slowly for a minute, the way the friends at Trier walked by the wall, and let one story of someone who changed come to mind. Ask it one question: what am I still saying not yet to? Then sit, and let the answer stay as it comes.
Ponticianus' story. A visitor's tale of two court officers who changed in an afternoon, and Augustine, still saying not yet.
Your line: why not now? Augustine is about to ask it out loud. Catch you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Christians have passed on the lives of saints like Antony to encourage one another, and churches differ on whether they ask people to name a moment of decision or speak of faith growing over a lifetime.

fork.setup: a church friend says real faith has a moment you can name. yours grew slowly. state her view at its strongest.
options: slow faith doesn't count, so yours isn't real faith.
'not yet' can quietly mean no; a now gets you off the fence.
moments are just more exciting to tell in church.
fork.reveal: that's the best case for the moment: Augustine's own 'not yet' was stalling. the slow view has one too: his years of circling counted.

original.note: Latin: look, now I become one. the court officer's words in Confessions 8.6: a friend of God, if I want it, ecce nunc fio.

trapdoor: what you thought: conversion is always one sudden moment.
what it means: two officers changed in an afternoon, while Augustine kept praying 'not yet'.
what a scholar hears: the officer's ecce nunc fio, look, I become one now, sets up Augustine's own why not now? in the garden of 8.12.

recall: bent for work, released to rest

chat.says: youth pastor wants my senior testimony sunday: 'the moment you knew.' i don't have a moment?? just... years.
options: Tell the true one. Faith can come in a moment or over years; both count.
Pick a day and call it the moment. A testimony needs a turning point.
Then you're not there yet. Wait until you have a real moment to share.
chat.meaning: Ponticianus' friends changed in an afternoon; Augustine circled for years. Christians tell both kinds of story. Tell yours as it was.

Ponticianus.meaning: a fellow African at the emperor's court who visits Augustine

Milan.meaning: a city in northern Italy, where Augustine was living

Trier.meaning: a city where the emperor was staying, in the story

testimony.meaning: telling others, often in church, how faith came to you

notes: All Confessions lines are paraphrased (quoted: null); the Pusey (1838) wording was not checked word for word.

Story beats from 8.6: Ponticianus 'a countryman of ours, so far as being an African', in high office at court; the book of the apostle on a gaming table; Antony unknown to them; at Trier, he and three companions walking during the afternoon circus games; two find the life of Antony in a cottage of servants of God; 'a friend of God, if I wish, behold, I become now'; both stayed. Confirm each, including the count of companions.
From 8.7: God 'setting me before my face' while Ponticianus spoke; the old prayer 'give me chastity and continency, only not yet'. 'Self-control' renders continence; confirm.
The house in Milan: 8.6 places the visit at Augustine's lodging where he and Alypius were; confirm 'his house in Milan' is fair.

v3 debate shape: the two views are faith told as a moment you can name and faith told as growth over a lifetime; both are described as views some churches hold, without naming or ranking churches. A Keeper may want named examples (e.g. a 'decision' testimony tradition; Orthodox and Catholic language of lifelong growth) if they can be put fairly.
Latin 'amicus autem dei, si voluero, ecce nunc fio' (8.6.15): confirm spelling and pronunciation (ecclesiastical vs classical).
The carry 'why not now?' anticipates Augustine's cry in 8.12; the lesson leaves that line for tomorrow ('Augustine is about to ask it out loud').
